item.title: Zero-shot de novo design of a metalloenzyme.
item.abstract: De novo design of enzymes is a frontier challenge, requiring consideration of catalytic mechanism and optimization across biochemical and biophysical criteria. Here, we present dEVA (design by EVolutionary Algorithm), a multi-objective protein design method built on principles drawn from evolutionary biology. We apply dEVA to the zero-shot, de novo design of metalloenzymes by optimizing the coordination sphere of catalytic metals. We characterize a bi-zinc metalloenzyme that exhibits promiscuous hydrolytic activity towards both phosphomonoesters and phosphodiesters. This design achieves a rate enhancement ((kcat/KM)/kw) of up to 3 x 1013 relative to the uncatalyzed reaction, comparable to characterized natural phosphatases. Structural characterization via x-ray crystallography and absorption spectroscopy supports the design of a de novo active site. These results demonstrate that de novo enzymes can be designed without pre-specified motifs, natural templates, or evolutionary information.

item.title: AlphaInterp: Revealing how AlphaFold 3 processes structure, confidence, and evolutionary information.
item.abstract: How does evolutionary information become structural knowledge? AlphaFold 3 predicts protein structures and biomolecular assemblies with remarkable accuracy, yet how it transforms comparative sequence information into three-dimensional structure remains poorly understood. Here, we use mechanistic interpretability to follow this transformation through AlphaFold 3 and identify a computational principle underlying its structural inference. By extracting single- and pair-representations across the model's forward pass and combining representational-geometry analysis, linear probing, activation patching, and perturbation of the multiple-sequence alignment (MSA) and its phylogenetic diversity, we show that AlphaFold 3 does not simply infer structure from raw sequence nor from MSA depth. Instead, a small number of sufficiently divergent homologues provides enough comparative information to largely recover the structure predicted using the full MSA. The pairformer transforms this evolutionary signal into a compact latent space in which residue-pair distances, contacts, fold similarity, and structural confidence become progressively decodable. Removing the MSA disrupts these latent geometries. Replacing it with evolutionarily similar homologues provides substantially less information, while evolutionarily unrelated sequences fail to rescue prediction despite preserving the formal alignment input. In contrast, phylogenetically diverse MSA subsampling largely restores both prediction accuracy and representational coherence. These results suggest that AlphaFold 3 has learned to infer structure by constraining its geometric priors and structural hypotheses by the sequence variation of the MSA. This framework helps explain both the model's remarkable predictive power and its characteristic failure modes, with direct implications for protein design, conformational diversity, out-of-distribution generalization, and the interpretation of model confidence.

item.title: Spliceosomal intron-free eukaryotic cells: rethinking the evolutionary significance of introns and the spliceosome.
item.abstract: Spliceosomal introns are important components of eukaryotic genomes, occurring widely within protein-coding genes and being removed through splicing during RNA maturation. Spliceosomal intron removal has long been considered an important foundation of eukaryotic gene expression regulation and cellular function, and has also been proposed as a potential driver of eukaryotic evolution. All extant free-living eukaryotes are known to contain spliceosomal introns. However, whether introns and the spliceosome are essential for the survival of eukaryotic cells remains a fundamental question in biology. In recent years, advances in synthetic biology and genome engineering have provided new strategies for exploring the fundamental components of eukaryotic life. Through synthetic genome design and systematic genome minimization, recent studies have demonstrated that Saccharomyces cerevisiae can survive in the complete absence of all known spliceosomal introns, indicating that spliceosomal introns are not genetic elements essential for yeast viability, and that the spliceosome is likewise not a molecular machine required for yeast survival. This finding challenges the conventional understanding of spliceosomal intron function and spliceosome essentiality, provides a new perspective on the evolutionary significance of introns, and offers guiding principles for the rational design and construction of synthetic eukaryotic genomes. This review systematically summarizes the types and multifaceted functions of introns, with a focus on the construction, viability, and fitness cost of the spliceosomal intron-free Saccharomyces cerevisiae strain SYNE27α, as well as evidence that the spliceosome is dispensable in this context. It further discusses the implications for the evolutionary retention of introns and the construction of minimal eukaryotic genomes.

item.title: Synthetic biology for improving photosynthesis.
item.abstract: Photosynthesis is the primary source of energy and matter for nearly all life on Earth, and its efficiency directly determines crop growth and yield. Synthetic biology offers a systematic engineering framework to enhance photosynthetic capacity by enabling rational design, standardized assembly, and iterative optimization of biological components. This review summarizes recent progress in applying synthetic biology to improve photosynthesis, with emphasis on modular design of genetic parts, construction of functional modules and genetic circuits for photosynthetic engineering. We discuss strategies organized by spatial scale, covering chloroplast-targeted interventions such as ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (Rubisco) optimization, photorespiratory bypasses, artificial carbon fixation cycles, and CO₂-concentrating mechanisms; cellular-level efforts to install C4 photosynthetic features into C3 crops; whole-plant manipulations of sugar transport and signaling to coordinate source-sink relations; and smart canopy designs to improve light utilization. Finally, we discuss the significance of closing the design-build-test-learn cycle for translating laboratory designs to field performance, which will help accelerate the application of photosynthetic engineering for sustainable crop improvement.

item.title: Base editor tiling of the PTPN11 gene identifies resistance variants to SHP2 inhibitors.
item.abstract: SHP2, a tyrosine phosphatase and key modulator of oncogenic signaling pathways, has emerged as a promising cancer target, but the impact of SHP2 mutations on therapy response remains unclear. Here we perform high-throughput mutagenic base editor screens in lung cancer cells to identify SHP2 mutations conferring resistance to migoprotafib and TNO155. Our screens identify numerous gain-of-function mutations associated with Noonan syndrome and various malignancies. Most resistance mutations overlap between inhibitors, although some exhibit elevated resistance to TNO155 compared to migoprotafib. Cross-referencing comprehensive genomic profiling data from predominantly advanced, SHP2 inhibitor-naive tumors reveals significant overlap between screen-enriched and tumor-associated mutations. We validate select mutations using in vitro and in cellulo assays and perform structural analyses to gain insights into the mechanisms driving resistance. Our study provides a comprehensive map of SHP2 mutations that reduce inhibitor sensitivity and identifies pre-existing variants that may confer intrinsic resistance to allosteric inhibitors in patients.

item.title: Decorating Bacteria With Electrostatically Bound Liposomes as Programmable Extracellular Functional Compartments.
item.abstract: Living cells are powerful programmable systems, yet efforts to engineer them are limited by the constraints of genetic modification, including metabolic burden, restricted chemical diversity of biomolecular systems, and slow, gene expression-driven responses. Complementary approaches augmenting cells without altering their genome offer an attractive route to expand their functionality. Here, we establish a strategy for equipping bacteria with synthetic extracellular organelle-like compartments by electrostatically assembling liposomes onto the surface of Escherichia coli. This approach yields stable, multi-compartment, high-density coatings without genetic or covalent modification, while preserving bacterial growth, gene expression, and motility. We show that these surface-bound liposomes can function as modular compartments that operate alongside the cell, enabling capabilities that are difficult to realize genetically, including thermoresponsive cargo release and abiotic catalytic activity. Together, this work shows that bacteria-liposome biohybrids can be engineered with appended, tunable synthetic compartments to expand the functional repertoire of living cells.

item.title: SynAb: Interpretable heavy-light chain synergy modeling for generalizable antibody-antigen interaction prediction.
item.abstract: Accurate prediction of antibody-antigen interactions (AAIs) is essential for therapeutic antibody discovery and high-throughput antibody screening. However, existing sequence-based methods often model antibody heavy and light chains independently, overlooking their cooperative contribution to antigen recognition. In this study, we propose SynAb, a synergy-guided cross-attention framework that integrates heavy-light chain regional cooperation into antibody-antigen interaction modeling. SynAb captures cooperative information across antibody functional regions and uses it to guide the interaction between antibody and antigen representations. Experimental results on the HIV and CoV-AbDab datasets demonstrate that SynAb outperforms the evaluated sequence-based methods and exhibits strong generalization in challenging scenarios involving unseen antibodies, unseen antigens, and previously unobserved antibody-antigen pairs. Beyond its predictive performance, SynAb explicitly characterizes the coordinated roles of paired heavy and light chains in antigen recognition. Moreover, without residue-level contact supervision, the model consistently highlights heavy-chain CDR-enriched regions, particularly CDR-H2 and CDR-H3, providing interpretable evidence consistent with established immunological knowledge. Together, these findings establish SynAb as a robust and interpretable framework for sequence-based AAI prediction and a promising computational tool for candidate prioritization in therapeutic antibody screening and synthetic biology applications.

item.title: Biosynthesis of a rare ginsenoside Compound K in engineered Ganoderma lucidum.
item.abstract: Ginsenoside Compound K (CK) is a rare protopanaxadiol-type ginsenoside with notable bioactivities. Production of CK via biotransformation remains limited by several challenges, including insufficient enzyme stability, high production costs, and poor catalyst reusability, which substantially hinder efficient production and restrict its large-scale application. Here, we report the first heterologous production of CK in Ganoderma lucidum, a medicinal macrofungus with an active triterpenoid biosynthetic pathway. Constitutive promoters suitable for G. lucidum were screened and validated using an mCherry reporter, with the PGltrpC cassette showing stronger activity than Pgpd. A Golden Gate-based multigene assembly system was then established to construct the biosynthetic pathway of CK and introduce it into G. lucidum. Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry confirmed CK production in transgenic strains, and the effect of LaeA overexpression on yield was evaluated. This work expands the genetic toolbox for G. lucidum and supports its use as a chassis for sustainable production of medicinal natural products.

item.title: Base editing in livestock and aquaculture: from tool development to breeding application.
item.abstract: The growing recognition of base editing as a precise genome-engineering strategy for single‑nucleotide conversions without double‑strand breaks has increased interest in its application to animal agriculture, where many economically important traits are influenced by single nucleotide variants. Although recent engineering efforts have broadened the targeting scope, improved editing precision, and reduced off‑target activity, major challenges remain in translating these tools to livestock and aquaculture species, particularly with respect to delivery, mosaicism, germline transmission, and breeding-scale deployment. In this review, we outline the development of cytosine, adenine, dual, and mitochondrial base editors, and discuss their advances in livestock and fish, including trait-oriented editing in pigs and cattle, rapid functional validation in model fish, and early proof-of-concept studies in aquaculture species. We further discuss the emerging potential of mitochondrial DNA base editing for animal breeding and evaluate the extent to which current advances support the broader goal of precision breeding and sustainable animal production.

item.title: Navigating the Drought Tolerance-Yield Trade-Off in Triticeae Cereals: From Molecular Networks to Climate-Resilient Breeding.
item.abstract: Drought driven by climate change severely threatens food security, particularly for wheat and barley grown in water-limited regions. A major breeding challenge is the trade-off between drought tolerance and yield. This review synthesises current knowledge of drought adaptation mechanisms in Triticeae crops, focusing on the transcriptional cascades, ABA-centric hormonal signalling and posttranslational modifications (kinases, phosphatases and ubiquitination) that confer resilience while often constraining carbon allocation to developing grains. Recent genomic advances, including genome-wide association study (GWAS), multi-omics integration and single-cell RNA-transcriptomics, have uncovered a wealth of drought-associated loci, although their translational potential is limited by data heterogeneity, environmental dependency and a persistent gap between laboratory validation and field performance. Emerging breeding approaches, such as speed breeding, wild-allele introgression, multiplex CRISPR/Cas9 and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven phenotyping are accelerating the development of climate-smart cultivars. Tissue-specific and inducible expression systems show early promise in uncoupling stress protection from growth penalties. Looking ahead, we propose that overcoming the yield-tolerance trade-off will require integrating synthetic biology, explainable AI, systematic exploration of novel variation and field phenomics coupled with digital twin modelling. Collectively, this review provides a strategic framework for engineering next-generation, climate-smart Triticeae cereals capable of maintaining productivity under intensifying drought conditions.

item.title: Cell-free RNA signatures derived from the tumor microenvironment predict outcomes of CAR T therapy in large B cell lymphoma.
item.abstract: Anti-CD19 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy can induce durable remission in patients with large B cell lymphoma (LBCL), yet outcomes remain variable. Reliable pre-treatment predictors of durable response remain limited, leaving a critical gap in patient management. To address this, we profile pre-treatment plasma cell-free RNA (cfRNA) from 91 LBCL patients treated with axicabtagene ciloleucel. We demonstrate that signatures of "lymph node-like" tumor microenvironments (TMEs), previously identified in tumor biopsies and shown to correlate with favorable outcomes, are elevated in the pre-treatment plasma cfRNA of responders, but not in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs). Using unbiased approaches, we identify additional cfRNA signatures associated with 1-year clinical outcomes that capture the underlying biological landscape of treatment response. Collectively, these findings support that pre-treatment plasma cfRNA could serve as a minimally invasive surrogate of TME state to potentially inform CAR T cell therapy outcomes and support risk stratification and TME-modulating adjunct therapies.

item.title: Early Detection of Ovarian Cancer: Current Strategies and Future Directions.
item.abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) is a major cause of cancer-related mortality among women worldwide, mainly because most cases are diagnosed at advanced stages due to non-specific early symptoms. Although early detection is essential for improving clinical outcomes, accurate and accessible screening remains a major challenge, owing to the non-specific nature of early symptoms, the pronounced histological and molecular heterogeneity of the disease, and the poor performance of conventional screening approaches based on cancer antigen 125 (CA-125), human epididymis protein 4 (HE4) and imaging modalities. This review outlines the major biological and technical challenges in the early diagnosis of OC, briefly summarizes the value and limitations of conventional diagnostic approaches and focuses on current progress in emerging biomarkers, including circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA)/cell-free DNA (cfDNA) alterations, exosomal biomarkers and mesothelin multi-marker combined detection strategies, and novel technologies, such as artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, single-cell sequencing and biosensors for early detection. We also discuss the advantages, current limitations, practical considerations and translational barriers of these approaches. Future advances in OC screening will require the integration of sensitive biomarkers, multimodal detection strategies and more accessible, cost-effective technologies to improve early diagnosis and patient survival.

item.title: Circulating biomarkers in early-stage hepatocellular carcinoma for risk stratification, diagnosis and prognosis.
item.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide, largely due to tumor heterogeneity, late diagnosis, and high recurrence rates even after curative treatment. Although HCC is potentially curable when detected at an early stage, suboptimal surveillance, particularly in patients with underlying cirrhosis or metabolic risk factors, limits the proportion of patients eligible for curative therapies. Current surveillance strategies for at-risk populations have intrinsic limitations, and the performance of imaging and serum biomarkers remains suboptimal. Moreover, the lack of reliable prognostic biomarkers for detecting early recurrence hampers post-treatment surveillance and impacts clinical outcomes. In this context, circulating biomarkers have emerged as promising tools for improving both early detection and prognostic stratification. Liquid biopsy has the potential to enable early, non-invasive diagnosis of HCC and allows longitudinal assessment of tumor progression through serial sampling. In early-stage HCC, blood candidates may complement or outperform conventional approaches by enabling earlier diagnosis and more accurate risk stratification. In this review, we summarize recent advances and current challenges in the clinical translation of circulating biomarkers. We focus on key liquid biopsy components, including circulating cell-free DNA, particularly circulating tumor DNA, circulating tumor cells, non-coding RNAs, extracellular vesicles, proteins and metabolites, such as bile acids and lipids, highlighting their diagnostic and prognostic potential and their possible integration into personalized management strategies for patients with early-stage HCC.

item.title: AI-assisted liquid biopsy for early breast cancer detection: a laboratory translation framework for future multimodal integration.
item.abstract: Early breast cancer detection is imaging-dependent in clinical laboratory medicine, and there are important limitations for interval cancers and women with dense breasts. Liquid biopsy is being developed as an adjunct to imaging and tissue diagnosis. There are two classes of circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) features and a separate class of extracellular vesicle (EV)-associated biomarkers, such as microRNAs, long non-coding RNAs, and proteins, to consider in the proposed framework. These literature reviews primarily focus on combinations of individual modalities, cfDNA-only combinations, cfDNA-protein panels, and multicancer models. There is a lack of prospective clinical validation of a machine learning model that integrates all three modalities for the early detection of breast cancer. We categorized performance evidence based on the purpose of the test for average-risk screening, dense breast triage, symptomatic assessment, high-risk surveillance, recurrence monitoring for breast cancer, and metastatic disease detection, and differentiated between direct breast cancer evidence and indirect methodological analogies. Translation involves modality-specific specimen processing, modality-specific analytical and clinical validation, locked/version-controlled pipelines, patient-, site-, and time-level data partitioning, leakage control, pre-specified thresholds and abstention rules, calibration assessment, external validation, subgroup analyses, reportable quality-control metrics, and defined revalidation triggers.

item.title: Combination of environment-responsive growth and stochastic growth initiation shapes population establishment dynamics in the ammonia-oxidizing bacterium Nitrosomonas sp. PY1.
item.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Many environmental bacteria do not readily grow under laboratory conditions, and population establishment often occurs stochastically. Although the scout hypothesis has been proposed to explain stochastic population establishment in environmental bacteria, how stochastic population establishment is shaped by individual cell growth behaviors in environmental isolates remains unclear. Here, we focused on the ammonia-oxidizing bacterium Nitrosomonas sp. PY1 and showed that environmentally responsive individual cell growth behavior combined with stochastic growth initiation shapes both deterministic and stochastic population establishment. Replicate cultivation revealed that PY1 exhibited stochastic population establishment, whereas the addition of its own cell-free supernatant (CFS) induced synchronous population establishment. Using single-cell observations, we found that PY1 exhibited ΔVt-dependent changes in individual cell growth behavior, where ΔVt represents instantaneous biomass production per unit volume. These ΔVt-dependent changes were suppressed by the addition of cell-free supernatant, suggesting that cell-derived compounds in the supernatant may modulate individual cell growth behavior in PY1. An individual-based model incorporating ΔVt-dependent individual cell growth behavior could describe the synchronous population establishment of PY1 in the presence of cell-free supernatant. By contrast, describing stochastic population establishment in the absence of cell-free supernatant required the additional incorporation of ΔVt-independent stochastic growth initiation following a Weibull distribution. These results suggest that the combination of ΔVt-dependent cell growth behavior and ΔVt-independent stochastic growth initiation can lead to deterministic or stochastic population establishment in PY1. Such environmentally responsive changes in population establishment dynamics may contribute to the low isolation success of environmental bacteria and sudden blooms of the rare biosphere.
IMPORTANCE: Many environmental bacteria establish populations stochastically under laboratory conditions, but how individual cell behavior shapes stochastic population establishment remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigated the ammonia-oxidizing bacterium Nitrosomonas sp. PY1 using single-cell observations and quantitative modeling. We found that its own culture supernatant synchronized population establishment timing and altered individual cell growth behavior. Furthermore, simulations based on observed single-cell behavior could describe synchronous population establishment dynamics in the presence of supernatant. However, describing heterogeneous population establishment dynamics in the absence of supernatant required the incorporation of stochastic growth initiation. These findings suggest that understanding population establishment dynamics in PY1 requires consideration of both environmentally responsive cell growth behavior and stochastic growth initiation. This study provides a quantitative framework linking individual cell behavior to stochastic population establishment in environmental bacteria and may help explain the low cultivation success and sudden blooms of rare environmental microorganisms.
